sections.content: Spokane, Washington doesn't make national headlines the way Seattle or Phoenix do, but savvy investors have been quietly stacking deals here for years. With home prices well below the national average, a growing population, and strong rental demand driven by two major universities, Spokane offers a rare combination of affordability and cash flow potential. Whether you're a seasoned wholesaler, a first-time flipper, or a landlord building a portfolio, finding real estate deals in Spokane WA is more achievable than you might think. If you're new to the game, start with our [Real Estate Investing for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/real-estate-investing-for-beginners) guide before diving into the Spokane-specific strategies below.
Spokane WA Market Overview: Why Investors Are Paying Attention

Spokane is Washington State's second-largest city, with a metro population of around 600,000 people. It sits in Eastern Washington, far removed from the sky-high prices of the Puget Sound region. The city has seen consistent population growth over the past decade, fueled by remote workers fleeing expensive coastal markets, students attending Washington State University and Gonzaga University, and a steady influx of retirees drawn to Spokane's affordable cost of living and outdoor recreation. This population growth has tightened housing inventory and pushed rents higher, creating favorable conditions for investors on both the buy-and-hold and value-add sides of the market.
Average Home Prices in Spokane WA

As of late 2024, the median home price in Spokane sits around $310,000 to $330,000, a significant increase from the $220,000 range seen in 2020, but still dramatically lower than Seattle's median of over $800,000. Single-family rentals in Spokane typically rent for $1,200 to $1,800 per month depending on size and location. For investors using the 1% rule as a quick screen, deals can still be found, particularly in older neighborhoods with distressed or dated properties. The price-to-rent ratio in Spokane is far more favorable than most West Coast cities, which is exactly why out-of-state investors have been flooding into the market. You can run your own numbers quickly using our free [Deal Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/wholesale-deal-calculator) to see if a specific Spokane property pencils out.
Best Neighborhoods for Real Estate Investors in Spokane

Not every zip code in Spokane offers the same opportunity. The city has a mix of established neighborhoods, transitional areas with strong upside, and some pockets best avoided by new investors. Here's a breakdown of the areas generating the most investor activity right now.
South Hill

South Hill is one of Spokane's most desirable residential areas. Homes here are well-maintained, schools are strong, and demand from both buyers and renters remains high. For flippers, South Hill offers the right environment to maximize after-repair value (ARV). Cosmetic rehabs on 1950s and 1960s ranch-style homes can yield solid spreads when purchased right. Use our free [ARV Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/arv-calculator) to estimate post-renovation values before making offers in this neighborhood.
East Central and West Central

These two neighborhoods offer the most opportunity for wholesale and value-add investors. Prices are lower, properties are older, and motivated sellers are easier to find. Both areas have seen revitalization efforts in recent years, and investor activity is increasing. Crime rates have historically been higher here, so do your due diligence, but experienced investors are finding some of the best wholesale deals in Spokane WA in these zip codes.
Garland and Emerson-Garfield

These north-side neighborhoods are experiencing a slow but steady gentrification. Small bungalows and craftsman homes are being renovated and resold at strong margins. Young professionals and students are driving rental demand here, and walkable commercial districts add long-term appeal. This is a strong area for both flipping and long-term buy-and-hold investing.
Spokane Valley

Technically a separate city, Spokane Valley functions as a suburban extension of Spokane and is a hotbed for rental property investors. Median prices are slightly lower than core Spokane, and the area has excellent access to employment centers and retail. Single-family rentals here tend to attract long-term tenants, reducing turnover costs for landlords.
Types of Real Estate Deals Available in Spokane WA
Wholesale Deals

Spokane has a healthy wholesale ecosystem. With a large stock of aging housing, probate situations, pre-foreclosures, and absentee owner properties, there's consistent deal flow for wholesalers who know how to find motivated sellers. Learning [how to find off-market real estate deals](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/off-market-real-estate-deals) is essential in this market, since many of the best opportunities never hit the MLS. If you're new to the wholesale model, our [Wholesaling Real Estate for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/wholesaling-real-estate-for-beginners) guide will walk you through the process from first offer to assignment fee.
Fix and Flip

Spokane's housing stock skews older, which means plenty of cosmetic and structural rehab opportunities. Flippers targeting the $250,000 to $350,000 purchase range with $30,000 to $60,000 in renovations can often sell into the $380,000 to $430,000 range in desirable neighborhoods. Labor costs in Spokane are lower than Seattle, which helps protect margins. That said, material costs have risen since COVID, so accurate rehab budgeting is critical. Always know your numbers before you make an offer.
Rental Properties

Spokane is a landlord-friendly state overall, and the rental market remains strong. Vacancy rates citywide hover around 4 to 5 percent, and with two universities generating consistent tenant demand, multi-family properties near campus commands premium rents. Duplexes and small apartment buildings in the $400,000 to $700,000 range are popular entry points for out-of-state investors looking to build passive income.

Pro Tip: When analyzing rental properties in Spokane, factor in heating costs. Eastern Washington winters are colder than the coast, and older homes with oil or electric baseboard heat can spike your tenants' utility bills — which affects tenant quality and retention. Look for properties with updated HVAC or gas forced-air systems whenever possible.
Spokane Real Estate Market Trends to Watch in 2024

items: Inventory remains tight: Active listings are still below pre-pandemic norms, keeping upward pressure on prices even as interest rates have slowed buyer activity.

Remote worker migration continues: Spokane attracted significant inflow from Seattle, the Bay Area, and Portland, and this trend has not fully reversed despite return-to-office mandates at some companies.
New construction is increasing: Developers are adding inventory in Spokane Valley and outlying areas, which may soften prices in certain submarkets over the next 18 to 24 months.
Rental demand is strong: Vacancy rates remain low and average rents have climbed 20 to 25 percent since 2020, making buy-and-hold strategies increasingly attractive.
Institutional interest is growing: Larger investors and regional operators are beginning to enter the Spokane market, signaling broader confidence in long-term fundamentals.

sections.content: The best time to invest in a market is before everyone else figures out it's a great market. Spokane is at that inflection point right now — strong fundamentals, affordable entry points, and growing institutional interest. The window for individual investors to get in at favorable prices is still open, but it won't be forever.
Practical Tips for Out-of-State Investors Targeting Spokane

Many of the most active investors in Spokane right now are buying from California, Texas, and other high-cost states. Remote investing is absolutely viable here, but it requires a smart approach. Knowing [how to analyze real estate deals like a pro](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/how-to-analyze-real-estate-deals) becomes even more important when you can't physically walk every property before making decisions.

items: Build a local team first: Before you buy, have a Spokane-based property manager, contractor, and real estate agent in your corner. Referrals from local investor groups are the fastest way to find reliable people.

Join the Spokane Real Estate Investors Association (SREIA): This local group hosts regular meetups and is a great way to network with local wholesalers, agents, and operators who know the market firsthand.

Use virtual tools to screen deals quickly: Platforms like AIWholesail can help you identify motivated sellers and undervalued properties across the Spokane market without requiring you to be on the ground every day.

Get pre-approved with a lender familiar with Washington State: Lending timelines and requirements vary by state. Work with a lender who understands Spokane's market conditions and won't slow down your deals.
Target absentee owners in the 99201 to 99208 zip codes: These core Spokane zip codes have high concentrations of older rental properties with absentee owners — a classic motivated seller profile.

Visit in person at least once before scaling: Even if you manage remotely long-term, an initial trip to walk neighborhoods, meet your team, and see properties firsthand will sharpen your market intuition significantly.

Study seasonal pricing patterns: Spokane's market tends to soften slightly in late fall and winter. Buyers face less competition from October through February, which can translate to better purchase prices.

sections.content: Pro Tip: When making offers sight-unseen in Spokane, always include an inspection contingency and budget conservatively for repairs. Eastern Washington has specific issues — including older galvanized plumbing, aging electrical panels, and foundation problems from freeze-thaw cycles — that can significantly affect your rehab budget if you're not prepared.

Spokane is one of the more accessible mid-size markets in the western United States for individual investors. The combination of relative affordability, genuine rental demand, and a growing population gives this market legs that many flashier markets lack. Whether you're looking for your first wholesale assignment or your tenth rental property, Spokane WA is worth serious attention in 2024.
